summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 2 diabetes, hypertension, chronic migraines, and multiple abdominal surgeries was admitted with a severe headache, right lower quadrant abdominal pain, and urinary symptoms. Evaluation revealed a urinary tract infection and constipation as key contributors to her presentation. She was treated with antibiotics for the infection and managed for constipation with laxatives and supportive care. Her migraine was treated symptomatically and improved with infection resolution. Abdominal imaging showed no obstruction, confirming a non-obstructive cause. She responded well to treatment, with resolution of symptoms, and was discharged home with a full antibiotic course, instructions for bowel management, and follow-up care. Her chronic conditions, including depression, hyperlipidemia, sleep apnea, and tobacco use, were noted but stable during admission.
